summary: Read Mitankin–Uhlemann arXiv:2411.02629v3 (JLMS): Thms 1.1–1.7 are Markoff-specific; only Thm 2.15 (≥2 finite-weight boundary components ⇒ WWA fails) is general, and it applies verbatim to ES because X_n: 4xyz = n·w(xy+yz+zx) ⊂ P³ has the same boundary as Markoff (triangle of lines w=0, xyz=0); the non-strict semi-integral HP is trivial there too ((0:0:1:1) ∈ D_1). Formulated the strict question: a primitive point (w:x:y:z) is a solution of 4/(nw) = 1/x+1/y+1/z, so strict Darmon-weight-2 points on D_1 are solutions of ES_{nq²} with the q-part only in x (gcd(q,yz)=1). Computed: for n = 9, 25, 49, 73, 97, 193, 409 such points are abundant (29–308 per q ≤ 13), so for n ≥ 2 the relaxation is vacuous and isolates nothing; at n = 1 (BM-obstructed per BL) Darmon-2 strict points = Type I solutions of odd squares, hence empty by T1 (checked w = 9…225), while Campana-2 points exist (w = 27, 125, 243, 343, 675, 1125). Calibration only: the n=1 obstruction survives exactly the square (Darmon) relaxation, i.e. it is T1; no transferable theorem for ES.
next: none for ES; optional one-line note that Darmon-2 strict points of the n=1 ES pair ⇔ Type I solutions of m² (T1).

summary: BRAINSTORM/invol_topological.md §3 already treats Smith theory: Lemma T (any finite mod-2 principle incl. Smith χ(K^G) ≡ χ(K) reduces to an odd weighted count = the open parity problem of memo (a), and is T1-killed if uniform) and Prop K (the canonical solution complex is homotopic to its incidence graph, parity-blind). Ran the item's first step anyway: complex on all ES words n' = tuv−u−v ≤ P (t,u,v ≥ 2) with faces = words sharing a letter; by the nerve lemma it is ≃ the letter/word incidence graph because two letters determine a word, so it is connected but b₁ = 2·#words − #letters + 1 (P = 5000: b₁ = 204 417; 4|t only: 43 553) — maximally far from ℤ/2-acyclic, for structural reasons that persist for any 'shared letter' face rule. Acyclicity would have to come from a different, p-dependent complex whose involution fixed set is certificates, which is exactly memo (a)'s open odd-count problem.
next: none unless a complex with a proved collapse (shelling) and certificate-valued fixed set is proposed.

summary: The item names no complex or moves, so instantiated it with the two natural fixed-p complexes: K(p) (vertices = denominators, 2-cells = solutions of 4/p; invol_topological.md Prop K) and a 'move' complex (vertices = solutions, edges/triangles = solutions pairwise sharing a denominator), and ran greedy elementary collapses via free faces. For p = 73, 97, 193, 409, 1201, 2521 (f = 6–15 solutions), K(p) collapses to c points (c = 1–5 components; b₁ = 0 at these sizes, consistent with Prop K b₁ = 2f−V+c). The move complex either collapses to the same c points or leaves a few critical cells (p = 73, 409) that only encode which solutions share a denominator. Collapses compress homology computations but cannot create certificates; any existence argument would need a p-uniform complex with a proved non-empty invariant, which is the Smith/parity situation already reduced in invol_topological Lemma T.

Borwein–Choi/xy+yz+zx is already compared with ES exceptional sets in BRAINSTORM/bsG_ternary_weinberger.md (E_W = {2,3,5,6,9,11,14,15,35,105,510} vs idoneal numbers; no fixed class group, so no Weinberger finiteness law) and z31_quadratic_forms.md §4, CONDITIONAL_ES.md ~l.282. Since ES has no failures, the only meaningful version of the step is the squarefree/squareful split of restricted-ES exceptional sets, done by factoring the repo's certified lists: U(n) (BREADTH_Z45.md l.265, n ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 10⁹) fails at all odd squares (squareful, structural T1) plus 105, 3985 = 5·797, 25305 = 3·5·7·241, 978145 = 5·7·27947 (squarefree) and 2961 = 3²·7·47, 111969 = 3³·11·13·29 (squareful); E_W has only 9 squareful. So the squareful part is the square obstruction and the sporadic tail is mostly squarefree (4/6, within the ≈ 0.8 squarefree share of odd n), mirroring A055745's squarefree finite-list pattern, with no extra clustering on square factors.

Reference-only catalog row; did the citation check. Mitsui, 'On the Goldbach problem in an algebraic number field I, II', J. Math. Soc. Japan 12 (1960) (II: pp. 325–372, verified via JMSJ index) proves the Vinogradov ternary theorem for large totally positive integers of a number field. Binary is only almost-all/density-type, and later work is the same (Giannitsi arXiv:2309.14249: ternary in sectors plus a density binary result; Knill arXiv:1606.05958: numerics/conjectures only). So the row's 'almost all, Hecke L-functions, power-many witnesses' is right for the binary analogue (the ternary one is pointwise for large n via circle-method power savings). As a calibration it adds nothing beyond rational Goldbach: power-size witness counts with the pointwise binary case still open, versus ES's polylog witness count. Contamination note: a repo git grep for 'mitsui' surfaced one line of a Pass-1 outcome script (scripts/z52b_p1_U09_outcomes_fix.py) for this item before I excluded those paths.

Covered by three memos. BRAINSTORM/gon_fermat_certificates.md (Anisotropic encodings (i)) reads Type I as ideal divisors of p+2c√−d in ℚ(√−d) and notes that Type I at level d needs (−d/p) = −1, so p is inert and the class group sees nothing of p. BRAINSTORM/bsB_rayclass_norm_pullback.md §2 PROVES that only norm-pulled-back characters χ∘N (Dirichlet characters mod the level) detect 'N𝔣 ≡ target (mod t)', with the single K-datum being the genus character, i.e. the sign/BM layer. CLASS_FORCING.md §2 Thm 2.1 shows the class of the total N is pure congruence data. Applied to the item: the order of discriminant −16d does not involve c, while the condition f ≡ −p (mod 4cd) does. The classes of the ideals above the prime factors multiply to the principal class of (p+2c√−d), which is no constraint, and Cl(−16d) meets the residue class of f only through genus characters mod 4d, already implied by the congruence. So 'class-group parity' can at most reproduce the genus/BM main term (which T1 shows is the square-exact layer) and cannot explain individual Type I failures; no computation beyond the cited scripts (scripts/bsB_genus_pullback.py) was needed.

Covered exactly. BRAINSTORM/z30_sl2_double_coset.md (SINGLE_P_COUNT §6, Prop 6.1, PROVED) shows the all-level count has one Γ_∞-double coset per level c, inside which b = p is the divisor problem of cp+1. Neither that nor the transposed picture produces Σ_c S(m,n;c) with fixed (m,n) over a long c-range, so Kuznetsov/θ never enters at fixed p. reviews/redteam-automorphic-2.md (~l.389) adds that even the Linnik–Selberg conjecture Σ_{c≤X} S(m,n;c)/c ≪ (mnX)^ε loses p^ε against the log²p main term, and bsG_modular_hyperbola.md / s8_volume_dfi.md give the n^{1/2} completion error (B3). Re-derived the first step: Σ_t D_t^−(tp+1) = #{(t,k,l): tkl−k−l = p} = #{(k,l): kl | p+k+l} = Σ_k #{m | p+k : m ≡ −1 (mod k)}. Completing the last congruence gives incomplete, divisor-restricted Kloosterman-type sums whose modulus is the shift k (the B2 tied modulus), not complete S(m,n;c) with p-fixed frequencies, matching the repo's conclusion; nothing new.

Did the plug-in. Treviño, JNT 149 (2015) Thm 1.2 (read from the author's PDF): for every prime p > 3 the least QNR satisfies g(p,2) < 0.9 p^{1/4} log p (p ≡ 1 (4)). For p ≡ 1 (8), ℓ(p) = g(p,2) (2 is a QR), so SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9 Prop 2.2 gives a BM-positive level 4 | t ≤ 4ℓ(p) < 3.6 p^{1/4} log p for every such p, with no lower threshold. Catch: for p ≡ 5 (8), g(p,2) = 2 and ℓ(p) is the least ODD prime QNR, which Treviño's theorem does not bound. Fix: if every odd n < y is a QR then χ(m + (p+1)/2) = −χ(2m+1) = −1 for 0 ≤ m < y/2, a constant string of length ≈ y/2, so ℓ(p) ≤ 2H + 1 with H the explicit max constant-string length (Treviño, Mosc. J. Comb. NT 2 (2012) 56–72, H < 1.55 p^{1/4} log p for p ≥ p₀ per its Table 1, plus a 2017 corrigendum; exact p₀ not checked). This gives t < 12.5 p^{1/4} log p for p ≥ 10²⁰ (CONDITIONAL on that range). Routine bookkeeping: the BM layer is already pointwise free and explains nothing about the divisor-class event, so it bears on ES only for formal or explicit-range write-ups.
next: if an explicit-range write-up is ever needed: confirm p₀ for H < 1.55p^{1/4}log p in Treviño 2012 + corrigendum.

summary: Covered by LOWERTAIL_ROUND2_FABLE.md §1.3 (Cor 1.2, PROVED; CERTIFIED at all 1 580 odd squares ≤ 10⁷) and SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9.md Prop 2.1(c). T1 for ES₅ is exactly six single-coordinate reciprocity facts: on every word the forced symbol (−u/A) or (−t/d) equals −1 for the divisor A ≡ −1 (mod u) (resp. d = tu−1 ≡ −1 (mod t)) with u or t ∈ 4ℤ ∪ (8ℤ+7), while at m² every divisor of m²+u or tm²+1 has symbol +1. The memo adds that the false-at-squares step is divisor-in-class existence, not character bookkeeping. Ran the item's computation (all words n ≤ 20 000 with level t ∈ 4ℤ ∪ (8ℤ−n)): (−t/(tu−1)) = −1 on all 89 590 words with 4 | t or t ≡ 3 (4) and odd tu−1, mixed (±1) for t ≡ 1 (4) (n ≡ 3, 7 (8)), and 0 words at odd squares. So the sought invariant is exactly χ_{−t}(d) = −1 (BL's Brauer class); it is constant on words at every non-square n too and realised at primes, so it is the known T1/BM layer, not a new conservation law.
